notes: FROZEN -- agent_supports=no, no phases. muse 1.2.1-R2847.1's only tool-free blocking dialog is the first-use workspace-trust prompt ("Do you trust this workspace?", live-verified via tmux capture-pane), and it is a delayed-birth startup gate -- the literal first thing the pane shows, before any ready/composer state. That is the same shape the already-catalogued codex and antigravity sibling cells for this row explicitly exclude (codex: "no working->waiting edge... only a delayed birth"; antigravity: "blocks BEFORE agy mints the conversation dir/transcript, so no session exists yet"), and both of those siblings keep agent_supports=yes only because they ALSO have a working, mid-session MCP elicitation trigger. muse has no such trigger: "elicitation" is entirely absent from the binary, and a full strings scan also found no sandbox/network-access confirmation dialog and no auto-mode/settings-review dialog ("auto-mode", "managed_settings", "settings review" all absent, unlike claudecode's literal dialog-registry strings for the same concepts). So muse has no dialog of this row's required shape at all. A coordinator review of this cell's first pass (which had reasoned agent_supports=yes/daemon_capability=incapable) asked whether the adapter's exact-filename skip of .session.jsonl.permission-init -- a hidden marker muse writes to the session directory before the trust decision -- was a buildable daemon gap rather than a genuine incapability. That question is answered fully in metadata.json's body: the marker IS durable (unchanged across 20+s while the dialog blocks, live-verified twice), carries the session's REAL final id (the directory name; confirmed because its content becomes session.jsonl's own first line, byte-for-byte, once trust is granted), does not linger on the happy path (consumed on trust grant), CAN orphan a directory forever if the process is killed before a decision (live-tested via kill -9), and is first-use-only per workspace (relaunching in an already-trusted cwd skips the dialog entirely, live-verified). Had a qualifying mid-session trigger existed for muse, recognizing this marker would have been a legitimate, non-guessing, buildable daemon extension (daemon=bug, not incapable) -- but no such trigger exists, so the daemon question is moot for this row. RE-ASSESS WHEN muse ships a mid-session, tool-free blocking dialog (most plausibly MCP elicitation, since an `mcp` OAuth subcommand already exists as a foundation); at that point apply the daemon-side reasoning already recorded in metadata.json's body directly.
